window.note: a phase write now records at the ticket's own address. Before this voyage NOTHING in the live system wrote a ticket file at all — grep for write_text/open(w)/json.dump against the tickets root across cairn/, skills/ and bin/ returned ZERO — so every cursor and phase across 259 tickets was a hand-edit, which is why 6bc43453ca64's :queued landed in cairn/tools/base/history.json: not the wrong address among several, the only address there was. set_phase(ticket=...) now appends to phase_writes and writes the rendered cursor and the top-level release back in the same act, with ONE clock shared by both addresses. THE SHAPE IS DETECTED, NOT IMPOSED, and that is a measurement that killed a chart hypothesis: the constrain packet asserted the corpus was indent=2/ensure_ascii=False with a trailing newline; a full-corpus round-trip found 208 ASCII-escaped with a newline, 44 non-escaped with one, and 8 non-escaped WITHOUT one. A writer picking any single shape reformats between 52 and 252 files to add three lines. 260 files round-trip byte-identical. THE FINDING WORTH CARRYING: mutant A (json.dumps(doc, indent=2), one shape imposed) SURVIVED the first cut of the teeth — the sandbox drew its fixture from the 207-file majority shape, so the tooth was measuring the mode and calling it the writer. The sandbox is now keyed by shape and fires the door once per shape the corpus holds. A caught mutant is the report; a mutant that had to be caught twice is the finding. STILL OPEN, RECORDED NOT BUILT: emit() only READS the ticket (transitions.py:330/878/1048) — it never writes it, so a CROSSING's ticket-side cursor is still a hand-edit, exactly as a phase write was before today. Out of this ticket's fills; owed its own ticket. Verdict artifact: 6/6 criteria pass, 6 dispositions (1 killed, 5 confirmed).
